item.title: ICE claim that man shattered skull running into wall triggers tension at Minnesota hospital
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS — Intensive care nurses immediately doubted the word of federal immigration officers when they arrived at a Minneapolis hospital with a Mexican immigrant who had broken bones in his face and skull. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents initially claimed Alberto Castañeda Mondragón had tried to flee while handcuffed and “purposefully ran headfirst into a brick wall,” according to court documents filed by a lawyer seeking his release.

item.title: Portland mayor wants ICE out after tear gas launched
item.description: PORTLAND — The city’s mayor demanded that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement leave his city after federal agents launched tear gas at a crowd of demonstrators — including young children — outside an ICE facility during a weekend protest that he and others characterized as peaceful.

item.title: Steven Spielberg wins first Grammy; ‘Kpop Demon Hunters’ earn genre’s first award
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The 68th annual Grammy Awards are taking place Sunday at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, and spirits were high from the jump after a few back-to-back, history-making moments.

item.title: Justice Department official plays down chance for charges arising from Epstein files revelations
item.description: WASHINGTON — A top Justice Department official played down the possibility of additional criminal charges arising from the Jeffrey Epstein files, saying Sunday that the existence of “horrible photographs” and troubling email correspondence does not “allow us necessarily to prosecute somebody.”

item.title: Mine collapses in eastern Congo, leaving at least 200 dead
item.description: GOMA, Congo (AP) — A landslide earlier this week collapsed GOMA, Congo — A landslide earlier this week collapsed several mines at a major coltan mining site in eastern Congo, leaving at least 200 people dead, rebel authorities said Saturday.several mines at a major coltan mining site in eastern Congo, leaving at least 200 people dead, rebel authorities said Saturday.

item.title: New U.S. charge d’affaires arrives in Venezuela to reopen diplomatic mission after 7 years
item.description: CARACAS — U.S. charge d’affaires Laura Dogu arrived in Caracas on Saturday to reopen the American diplomatic mission in Venezuela after seven years of severed ties.

item.title: Stunner in Texas as Democrat flips Republican state Senate district that Trump won by 17 points
item.description: Democrat Taylor Rehmet flipped a reliably Republican state Senate district in Texas in Saturday's special election, continuing a string of surprise victories for Democrats across the United States in the year since Donald Trump returned to the White House.

item.title: Trump says U.S. is ‘starting to talk to Cuba’ as he moves to cut its oil supplies
item.description: ABOARD AIR FORCE ONE — President Donald Trump said the United States was beginning to talk with Cuban leaders as his administration puts greater pressure on the communist-run island and cuts off key oil supplies.

item.title: Misconduct complaint dismissed against judge who handled El Salvador prison deportation case
item.description: WASHINGTON — A federal appeals court judge has dismissed a misconduct complaint filed by the Justice Department against a judge who clashed with President Donald Trump ’s administration over deportations to a notorious prison in El Salvador.

item.title: Politics are everywhere. Is the 2026 Super Bowl any different?
item.description: As the Seahawks prepare to play in their fourth Super Bowl, the NFL stands as the preeminent cultural force in an America that more and more seems to be tearing itself apart at the seams. The spectacle purports to rise above the political tumult and the scenes of horror that have engulfed the nation, but they can't help but be dragged into the din.
